title: agentscope-ai/agentscope — Build and run agents you can see, understand and trust.
content:
中文主页 | Documentation | Roadmap
AgentScope 2.0 is a production-ready, easy-to-use agent framework with essential abstractions that keep up with rising model capability.
We design for increasingly agentic LLMs. Our approach leverages the models' reasoning and tool use abilities rather than constraining them with strict prompts and opinionated orchestrations.
- [2026-10] FEAT: Voice profile management and voice cloning supported — select saved voices in chat, with DashScope and OpenAI voice cloning clients available in the Python SDK.
- [2026-10] FEAT Experimental: Agent service supports realtime voice conversations over WebRTC, with text and voice sharing the same session history.
- [2026-09] FEAT Experimental: SOP supported — run multi-step tasks as standard operating procedures, in both the framework and agent service. Docs | Service
- [2026-09] FEAT: TeamPipeline supported — a leader agent delegates tasks to member agents. Docs
- [2026-09] INTE: MiniMax chat models supported via MiniMaxChatModel (MiniMax-M3 by default).
- [2026-09] FEAT: Model routing supported — use ModelRouterMiddleware to select an appropriate chat model for each reply.
- [2026-09] INTE: Jev classifier model supported through the TypeSafe SDK via JevClassifierModel.
- [2026-09] FEAT: agentscope-skill now supports AgentScope v2.
- [2026-09] INTE: Support DashScope, OpenAI, Gemini and xAI realtime APIs in RealtimeAgent. Example | Docs
- [2026-09] FEAT Experimental: Realtime voice agent supported. Example | Docs
Welcome to join our community on
AgentScope requires Python 3.11 or higher.
uv pip install agentscope# Pull the source code from GitHub
git clone -b main https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope.git
# Install the package in editable mode
cd agentscope
uv pip install -e .
The SDK layer — compose an agent from a rich set of building blocks:
Start your first agent with AgentScope 2.0 in console:
from agentscope.agent import Agent
from agentscope.console import launch_console
from agentscope.tool import Toolkit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Read, Write, Edit
from agentscope.credential import DashScopeCredential
from agentscope.model import DashScopeChatModel
import os, asyncio
async def main() -> None:
    agent = Agent(
        name="Friday",
        system_prompt="You're a helpful assistant named Friday.",
        model=DashScopeChatModel(
            credential=DashScopeCredential(
              api_key=os.environ["DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"]
            ),
            model="qwen3.6-plus",
        ),
        toolkit=Toolkit(
            tools=[
                Bash(),
                Grep(),
                Glob(),
                Read(),
                Write(),
                Edit(),
            ]
        ),
    )
    # Chat with the agent in the terminal — streamed output, tool-call
    # confirmation and Ctrl+C interruption are all handled for you
    await launch_console(agent)
asyncio.run(main())
AgentScope ships a batteries-included agent service — a FastAPI backend with a pre-built Web UI (examples/web_ui) that turns your agents into a multi-tenant, multi-session application, with rich capabilities out of the box:
Everything above is composable, so you can assemble your own application on top of the service with minimal glue code.
Run the following commands to start the agent service backend and the web UI:
git clone -b main https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope.git
cd agentscope/examples/agent_service
# start the agent service backend
python main.py
Then open another terminal to start the web UI:
cd agentscope/examples/web_ui
# start the webui
pnpm install
pnpm dev

report.summary: Alibaba's AgentScope 2.0 relaunches as a production-ready agent framework with SDK building blocks plus a batteries-included FastAPI service and web UI for multi-tenant agent apps.
report.background: AgentScope first appeared in February 2024 as a research-flavored multi-agent platform from Alibaba's Tongyi Lab, followed by AgentScope 1.0 in 2025, which repositioned it as a developer-centric framework. Version 2.0 is a substantial rethink: instead of constraining models with rigid prompt templates and hand-wired orchestration graphs, it assumes LLMs are increasingly capable reasoners and gives them tools, memory and execution loops, leaning on the model's own planning. This mirrors a broader shift across the agent ecosystem, where frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI's Agents SDK and MCP-centered tooling are competing to become the default runtime. Notably, AgentScope ships a full application layer — multi-tenancy, sessions, a web UI — not just a library, and integrates tightly with Alibaba's DashScope/Qwen models while staying model-agnostic.
key_points: From library to platform: AgentScope 2.0 bundles an SDK layer of composable building blocks (Agent, Toolkit, tools like Bash, Grep, Glob, Read, Write, Edit, model and credential abstractions) together with a full agent service — a FastAPI backend plus prebuilt web UI that turns an agent into a multi-tenant, multi-session application with minimal glue code.

Model-agnostic integrations are widening fast: DashScope/Qwen, OpenAI, Gemini, xAI and MiniMax chat models are supported, along with realtime APIs in a RealtimeAgent, a ModelRouterMiddleware that picks a model per reply, and the experimental Jev classifier and MiniMax-M3 support.

Voice is a first-class feature: the roadmap adds voice profile management and voice cloning via DashScope and OpenAI clients, plus experimental realtime voice conversations over WebRTC where text and voice share one session history — unusual depth for an open agent framework.

Orchestration is optional, not mandatory: TeamPipeline lets a leader agent delegate to member agents, SOP mode runs multi-step tasks as standard operating procedures, and everything is composable so developers can assemble their own app on top of the service layer.

Licensing and ecosystem are developer-friendly: Apache 2.0, Python 3.11+, installable via uv pip, with published academic papers (AgentScope 1.0 and the original multi-agent platform paper) backing the design and a community contributor program.
report.impact: For the AI industry, AgentScope 2.0 signals that agent frameworks are converging on a full-stack shape: model integration, tool execution, memory, multi-agent delegation and a deployable application layer in one package. That puts pressure on thinner libraries to either specialize or add hosting. For developers, the appeal is pragmatic — a batteries-included FastAPI service and web UI remove weeks of multi-tenancy, session and streaming plumbing, while the model-agnostic router lowers vendor lock-in, though teams already invested in LangGraph or OpenAI's SDK face migration costs and should weigh ecosystem maturity and community size. For regular users, the visible payoff is more reliable long-running assistants that can actually use tools, handle voice natively, and follow structured procedures — features that make agent products feel less like demos and more like software.
report.tools: Try AgentScope directly (pip install agentscope, Python 3.11+), starting with the console example and then the agent_service plus web_ui examples. Worth comparing against LangGraph and CrewAI for orchestration, OpenAI's Agents SDK, Microsoft AutoGen, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool interoperability. If voice matters, prototype with WebRTC and OpenAI or DashScope realtime APIs; for local models, pair AgentScope with vLLM or Ollama as the chat-model backend.
